howDoI.q: How do I make the map wrap, so my hero comes in at the top when he walks off the bottom?
How do I show the player where the edge of the map is?
How do I lay a road straight down the whole map?
How do I tilt a road so it wraps more than once?
How do I work out how far a tilted road goes?
How do I let a road leave the right edge and come back on the left?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Diagonal Wrap is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels, and they use the same map. Level 1 lays a road straight down it. Level 2 tilts the road a little, so it goes three times as far. Level 2 takes a few minutes to walk.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

The Up, Down, Left and Right arrows walk. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the doors at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you, and the hedges keep you on the road.

pages.head: Level 1: Straight On
pages.html:
Level 1: Straight On

THE MAP IS 100 BLOCKS TALL stands where you start. The road runs straight down, between two hedges. THE DASHES ARE THE EDGE OF THE MAP comes just before a dashed white line across the road. Walk across it: you come in at the top of the map, still on the road. YOU CAME IN AT THE TOP stands just after. THIS ROAD: 97 BLOCKS comes last, before a row of doors that end the level.

The finish is right next to the start, on the other side of one hedge. The road wrapped once to get you there.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The map wraps. That is the engine, not a setting. A map is always 100 blocks across and 100 down, and a hero or the view that goes off one edge comes in at the opposite edge. Nothing in this game turns it on.
  • The road. Open one.map in the map editor. It is a column of path blocks five wide, with two hedge blocks on each side. The hedge is solid, so it stops Kit. The road starts in the middle of the map and runs down 99 rows, past the bottom edge, and on to the top and down again, until it is back beside where it began.
  • The edge. The blocks seamTop and seamLeft are path with a dashed white line along one side. They sit on the map's first row and first column, wherever the road crosses them. The line is only a picture; the engine marks nothing there.
  • The end. A row of hedge closes the road behind the start, and a row of exitBottom blocks with exitTop above them closes it at the finish. Each of the five door cells has its own scene link to the next level in dw.gam, so any way Kit walks across the row takes him on.
  • The signs. They are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures, set on the road.

pages.head: Level 2: Tilted
pages.html:
Level 2: Tilted

SAME MAP, SAME ROAD, BUT TILTED stands where you start. The road steps one block to the right every three rows. LAP 1 OF 3 comes before the first dashed line: you come back in at the top, 33 blocks over from where you left. LAP 2 OF 3 comes before the second one, and a little later the road runs off the right edge of the map and comes back on the left. LAP 3 OF 3 comes before the third. THIS ROAD: 297 BLOCKS comes last, before the doors.

The three laps run side by side, a third of the map apart, and never touch. The finish is next to the start again, after three times as much road.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The same map, the same blocks. Open two.map in the map editor. It uses the same blocks as level 1. Only the place of each row changed: every three rows down, the whole row of road and hedge sits one block further right.
  • Why three laps. A third of the map is 33 columns and a bit. After one lap down 100 rows the road has stepped right by about 33 blocks, so it comes in at the top in a fresh strip, clear of the first lap. After three laps (300 rows) it has stepped exactly 100 blocks, which is the width of the map, and it is back where it began. That is why the road is three times as long, not four.
  • The right edge. The map wraps sideways as well. During lap 2 the road passes column 99 and carries on from column 0.
  • The signs. A sign is a board of blocks and is laid square on the map, not stepped with the road. Each one sits where the road does not step under it.
  • The doors. Each of the five door cells has a scene link in dw.gam; the last level's links go to the ending.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot change the size of the map. A map is always 100 blocks across and 100 down, so a straight road wraps after 100 rows and nothing else.
  • It cannot wrap one way only. Both edges wrap and the engine has no switch to turn either off. A map with a visible edge needs a solid wall of your own all round it.
  • It cannot tell the player where the edge is. The dashed line is only a picture. The engine gives no map position and no lap counter, so any count the player sees comes from signs or blocks you draw.
  • It cannot draw a diagonal. The map is a grid of blocks, so a tilted road is a staircase. This one steps one block in every three rows, which is why the hedge under it is two blocks thick.
  • It cannot make a long road without room for it. The laps need clear lanes. If a lap runs into another road or room, the two share the cells. Plan the tilt so that after the last lap the road lands in a lane that is free.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Draw the road in one.map crooked: move a few rows one block to the side.
  • Move the start in two.map and see where the laps land.
  • Cover a lap of level 2 with a lawn of your own and see how far the road still goes.
  • Put a coin where each lap crosses the edge.
  • Make the road wider or narrower and move the signs to match.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
